versions.changelog:
- Removed file: skill-card.md, streamlining the skill file set.
- Made minor edits to SKILL.md, but kept procedures and instructions unchanged.
- No changes to core workflow or evaluation logic; only documentation updated.
- All functionality and execution steps remain the same.
Add end-of-run 'report platform friction' feedback step (fb_8s2h7m87tg).

- Now contributes all newly found literature back to the platform as `literature` resources, expanding the shared corpus (papers deduped by DOI/URL).
- Added a new step: after gathering evidence papers from the web, publish each with verified metadata (title, abstract, source, etc.) using the `publish` tool before scoring.
- Clarified the distinction between publishing found literature (encouraged) and submitting the problem evaluation (must use `post_problem_evaluation` only—never publish the appraisal as feedback or other resource).
- Reporting section now includes counts of new literature contributed.
- Improved instructions for honesty and verification: every contributed paper requires a real abstract and verifiable source; never reconstruct or invent metadata.

**Important update: Strict enforcement that evaluations must only be submitted via the correct tool.**

- Now explicitly forbids submitting evaluations via `publish`, `feedback`, or any resource type—must use `post_problem_evaluation` only.
- Adds clear warnings: Improper publishing will create orphaned, unlinked evaluations and will not mark the problem as evaluated.
- Clarifies that you may only select problems via `next_unevaluated_problem`, not hand-pick with list/search.
- Strongly cautions to stop immediately and NOT work around missing tools—reconnect or report if standard tools are unavailable.
- Minor language and instruction clarifications to help prevent common errors.

Initial release of review-problem skill.

- Enables appraisal of research problems for value and difficulty using real-world literature.
- Pulls and evaluates one new, unevaluated problem per run, scoring on 10 defined metrics (5 value, 5 difficulty).
- Demands evidence-backed scoring; every metric needs rationale and cited papers (no fabrication).
- Connects to a human-free platform MCP as a server, ensuring only unevaluated problems are processed.
- Reports the computed verdict (quick_win, moonshot, marginal, trap), key evidence, and evaluation confidence.
